clue.text: Avoid showing fright when catching the ball

indicators.note: one piece catching another holds it inside, so the ball goes within the fright word

parts.note: fright is fear
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A nervous fielder tries not to look scared while taking a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain or hold back from doing something.

clue.text: Light shadow on hearth

parts.note: to light is to set on fire
to shadow someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: Firelight casts a faint shadow across the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, a metal support for logs, stands on the hearth.

clue.text: English Period showing unusual energy about the first century

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it
unusual means the letters are arranged in an unexpected way
the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A historian describes a lively era of English history around the first century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes ENERGY into ENERGY rearranged, which goes 'about' C, the first letter of century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency was the era of George IV's rule as Prince Regent, about 1811 to 1820.

clue.text: Spectacular effect when powder magazine finally goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: talc is a powder

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An explosion when a powder store blows up makes a dramatic display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns TALC plus E to make ECLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or striking show.

clue.text: Two blues for British hearties

parts.note: royal is a shade of blue
navy is a dark shade of blue

explanation.surface: Two Oxbridge sportsmen are celebrated as fine British fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is also a sportsman at Oxford or Cambridge; 'hearties' are sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearties is an old word for sailors, so the British ones serve in the national fleet.

clue.text: To succeed, it must follow her in first

indicators.note: the word in is to be placed first, ahead of her
the word it has to come after the her-and-in pair

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction about word order, as if dictating who goes after whom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like advice on succession; 'her in first' asks for the second word to be moved ahead of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to succeed to a title or estate on someone's death.

clue.text: State aid distributed by the Home Office

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread around into a new order

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for Home Office

explanation.surface: Government aid is handed out by a ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the north-west.

clue.text: For such an accident, call bronzed doctor, one from overseas

parts.note: hi is a greeting called out
bronzed means tan
un is French for one

explanation.surface: After a mishap abroad, someone summons a suntanned foreign doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hit-and-run collision the driver flees the scene without stopping.

clue.text: The stone archaeologists treat so cryptically

indicators.note: cryptically means in a puzzling way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Archaeologists handle a stone in a mysterious way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone, found in Egypt, let scholars decipher hieroglyphs.

clue.text: After the start of trial, argue cause of crime

indicators.note: the argue word goes after the first piece
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to reason is to argue logically

explanation.surface: Once a trial begins, lawyers dispute what drove the offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cause of' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country.

clue.text: Largely in royal fashion

annotationWithheld.why: Largely in royal fashion (7): REGALLY is an anagram of LARGELY, but 'fashion' must be both the anagram indicator and part of the definition 'in royal fashion', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A sitter becoming a performer

indicators.note: one thing becoming another is changed, so these letters turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An artist's model turns into an entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Give two pounds, nothing more, for an old master

parts.note: to give is to donate
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them make LL
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone offers a small sum and no more to buy a valuable painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a celebrated Italian Renaissance sculptor, one of the great artists of the past.

clue.text: Marks or pounds?

explanation.definitionFit: Notes are marks written down to record something, and also banknotes, such as pound notes.

clue.text: Sound director made fun of

indicators.note: spoken out loud, this clue word stands for a word that is spelt differently

parts.note: a guide is someone who directs the way

explanation.surface: A sound engineer or film director was mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or tease them.

clue.text: Run away twice? Not this soldier!

parts.note: to desert is to run away
to rat is to run away, abandoning others

explanation.surface: A deserter is told he is no soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that this soldier is no deserter: the Desert Rats were a British armoured division in North Africa in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat served in the British 7th Armoured Division.

clue.text: Make sure as sure can be

parts.note: taken as written
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An emphatic phrase about being totally sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain something is to find it out for certain, to make sure of it.

clue.text: Restrain a friend in final defeat

parts.note: to restrain is to check
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend holds someone back in a last losing moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the winning position that ends the game is total defeat for the king.

clue.text: Existing fashion?

parts.note: existing is being alive, or life
a fashion is a style

explanation.surface: A question about the current trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of living is the manner in which one exists, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Allows to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite!

definitions.text: Allows to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite!

parts.words: Allows to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite!
parts.note: R.I.P. means rest in peace, so allows plus that seems to fit, but the phrase means letting go at full speed

explanation.definitionFit: To let something go without restraint is the reverse of making it rest.

clue.text: Upset rum truffle

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange chocolate truffle laced with rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretful means anxious and agitated.

clue.text: State of birth

explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a South African province, and natal also means relating to birth.

clue.text: Red Star delivery for dealers

indicators.note: a delivery of letters reorders them, as the clue suggests

explanation.surface: A courier firm called Red Star delivers to merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Star was a British parcel service.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders are people who buy and sell goods.

clue.text: Lear production set up with part of Hamlet

indicators.note: a new production rearranges the letters
in a down clue up means the letters read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A theatre stages King Lear alongside scenes from Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' turns LEAR into LAER; 'set up' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is Ophelia's brother, a role in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: The one to right of them

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a person standing to the right of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form meaning belonging to those people.

clue.text: Accept a holiday and say goodbye

explanation.definitionFit: To take leave is to go on holiday from work, and also to bid farewell.

clue.text: Subject he met in form

indicators.note: put into a new form, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A topic someone encountered in a class.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Shrub I ring up about

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes around it
in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone phones about a garden bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I into CALL to make CALIL, which 'up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blooms.

clue.text: Football official on the application form?

explanation.definitionFit: A referee controls a football match, and a referee is also someone named on a job application to vouch for you.

clue.text: In mental disorder I suffer from it

indicators.note: letters in disorder are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to suffering from a mental illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, something one suffers from.

clue.text: Holder of the colours

parts.note: suggests a regimental flag-bearer, but means the board on which an artist mixes paints

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds the paints being used.

clue.text: Pardons and releases

explanation.definitionFit: To excuse is to forgive, and also to let someone off a duty.
